subject: Deal: Datacore - GPU provisioning & switchover playbook
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@datacore.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: sizing inputs and swap window — Datacore Dedicated

Hi Elena / Marco —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a first-pass capacity model that maps your committed qps and 95th p95 token lengths into a conservative GPU pool: datacore_capacity_model_v3.xlsx. Key asks from our side to finalize the plan: 

- Confirm expected steady-state qps per route (list in sheet "Traffic")
- Confirm peak burst window (minutes) for promotional traffic
- Callout any multi-tenant isolation or region constraints (we noted EU data residency on page 2)

Proposed next steps: Ben will run a throughput profile against a 16GB quantized variant, and Karthik will produce a cutover window that minimizes user impact. If we can lock the traffic numbers by Friday, we can target a pilot swap week of Feb 6–10.

Attachments: datacore_capacity_model_v3.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0142

From: Elena Soto <elena@datacore.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@datacore.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-17T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: sizing inputs and swap window — Datacore Dedicated

Kimberly —

Thanks for the spreadsheet. Quick responses: 
- Steady-state qps: 240 requests/min for user-facing route, with average token length ~120; background batch embeddings are 60 qps but can be queued overnight if needed.
- Peak burst: marketing sends 30-minute blasts that can triple qps for ~20 minutes.
- Data residency: primary traffic is US, we will still have EU test traffic but not production.

Can Ben confirm whether the 16GB quantized variant covers the triple-burst without dropping below 200ms per-token SLO? If not, we may need a short-lived burst pool.

Also attaching our internal runbook excerpt for traffic patterns.

Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Datacore

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@datacore.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-18T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: sizing inputs and swap window — Datacore Dedicated

Elena / team —

I ran an initial local throughput sim against the customer's sample prompt set and a 16GB INT8-quant variant (profile attached inside the spreadsheet). Short summary: 
- With continuous batching and prefix KV cache enabled we hold ~220 qps steady at median per-token latency ~160ms; under a 3x burst and assuming the auto-burst pool is configured we approach 2.8x utilization which pushes p95 token latency toward 320ms.
- Recommendation: provision a 10% warm-burst headroom pool (2–3 additional cards) and enable short-lived burst autoscaling (60s ramp) to preserve the 200ms average SLO for user-facing route.

Concrete ask: can Datacore accept a 60s user-facing ramp (we'll throttle inbound at the edge to smooth spikes) and commit to the initial reserved capacity for Q1? If accepted, Karthik and I will draft a tight cutover playbook (dry-run, smoke validation, smoke rollback) and embed explicit quiesce windows.

Ben Carter
Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@datacore.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-19T14:02:00Z
Subject: Cutover playbook draft and proposed timelines — Datacore DC-2741

Hi all —

I've sketched a minimal cutover playbook below (full markdown attached as cutover-checklist.md):

1) Pre-flight (D-7 to D-3)
   - Confirm final traffic numbers and SRE contact roster (Datacore)
   - Provision reserved pool (X cards) in us-west-2 and validate kernel selection
   - Upload and pin model variant to reserved fleet (v3-int8-dc2741)

2) Dry-run (D-2)
   - Run synthetic traffic at 1.5x steady qps, validate KV cache warm-up and p95 latency under batching
   - Collect token-level traces and acceptance metrics (latency, errors, token-cost)

3) Cutover window (D0) — suggested midnight–04:00 PT low-traffic window
   - Ramp traffic 0% -> 50% -> 100% over 30–60 minutes
   - Smoke checks at each step, automatic rollback if errors >0.5% or p95 regression >2x

4) Post-cutover (D+1 to D+7)
   - Monitor signatures for regressions, keep burst headroom for 72 hours
   - Run targeted A/B quality checks on critical prompts

Proposed dates (dependent on signed SOW):
- Provisioning: Jan 24–26
- Dry-run: Jan 29
- Cutover week: Feb 6–10 (single chosen D0 during the week)

Please review and flag anything that would block the provisioning timeline. If Datacore is aligned, we can convert the draft SOW to a signed doc and schedule the provisioning window.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Elena Soto <elena@datacore.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-01-20T16:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Cutover playbook draft and proposed timelines — Datacore DC-2741

Karthik / Kimberly —

This looks good and conservative — we appreciate the explicit rollback gates. A few quick confirmations: 
- Datacore legal is clearing the SOW this week; procurement expects to sign by Jan 26.
- Ops accepts the 60s ramp and the 10% warm-burst recommendation. We request a single daylight rehearsal on Feb 2 with 1.25x traffic so our incident responders can run the runbook.

Please go ahead and mark Jan 24 for provisioning. I'll upload the signed SOW and routing ACLs once legal completes review.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Director, Platform Engineering
Datacore
